title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page holds a short handwritten note, written on the back of a typed Montpellier seminar announcement (Bensoussan, 'Diffusions réfléchies', 19 June 1975). It reads: 'M/Neg_∞ ≃ lim→ M_N, n'est pas une catégorie à lim→ filtrantes exactes.'

The likely context is the divided-power de Rham / crystalline cohomology computations on the neighbouring pages (Γ^*, maps H^{2i}(X,J) → H^{2iα}(X,Γ^α J), the relation x^i = i! x^{(i)}). These produce torsion denominators, such as factorials, that one wants to ignore 'up to bounded torsion'.

1. Setting. M is an abelian category of modules or sheaves over a base with a distinguished element π or p. Neg_N is the class of 'negligible of order N' objects, plausibly those killed by π^N (or by N!). Neg_∞ = ∪_N Neg_N is the class of objects killed by some unspecified but bounded power. This is a thick (Serre) subcategory.
2. Claim (i). The Serre quotient M/Neg_∞ is the 2-colimit (filtered union) of categories M_N. Each M_N formally inverts maps whose kernel and cokernel are N-negligible. So Hom in the quotient is the colimit over N of Hom_N.
3. Claim (ii). This quotient is not an AB5 category: it does not have exact filtered colimits. The reason is that Neg_∞ is not a localizing subcategory. An infinite direct sum ⊕ Z/p^n has unbounded torsion, so it is not negligible, although each summand is. Hence the quotient functor does not commute with infinite sums or filtered colimits, and exactness of filtered colimits fails.

The point serves as a caution. One cannot work naively 'modulo bounded torsion' as a Grothendieck abelian category, for instance to take derived functors or inductive limits of cohomology. This matters when comparing divided-power de Rham cohomology with ordinary cohomology up to uniformly bounded torsion.
errors: Gap: if Neg_N means 'killed by π^N', then Neg_N is not closed under extensions (an extension of objects killed by π^N is killed by π^{2N}). So M_N cannot literally be a Serre quotient. It must be defined as a 'Hom up to N' category, and only the union over N is well behaved. The page does not specify this.
The non-AB5 claim is correct in substance, but it is stated without proof. The quotient may even fail to have arbitrary sums computed naively.

ideas.what: The category of modules modulo bounded-torsion (negligible) objects, written as the filtered 2-colimit of categories 'up to N'.
ideas.modern_name: Serre quotient by a thick, non-localizing subcategory; category 'up to bounded torsion' / isogeny-type category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (classes of abelian groups, 1953); Gabriel (1962, quotient categories); Berthelot–Ogus and others used 'up to bounded torsion' statements in crystalline cohomology
ideas.where_published: Quotient categories appear in Tôhoku (1957) and Gabriel's thesis. The specific 'Neg_∞' formulation is not known to be published.

ideas.what: Observation that this quotient lacks exact filtered colimits, because negligible objects are not stable under infinite sums.
ideas.modern_name: Failure of AB5 for quotients by non-localizing Serre subcategories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Gabriel 1962: only localizing subcategories give Grothendieck quotients)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Tôhoku-style AB axioms and Gabriel's work.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a brief, correct, standard categorical remark: the quotient by bounded-torsion objects is not AB5. It is useful context for working 'up to bounded denominators' in divided-power de Rham cohomology, but it is not new.
transcription_corrections: The last word 'exactes' is written abbreviated, as 'ex..tes', in the manuscript.
'Neg_∞' (presumably 'négligeables') is handwritten 'Neg∞'. The colimit is written 'Lim' with an arrow underneath (lim→), applied to M_N.
The verso shows the reversed show-through of the typed 1975 seminar announcement. The page number '253' is pencilled at the bottom left.
